newsitem.title: USA: Nike recalls shoes that offend Muslims.
newsitem.headline: Nike recalls shoes that offend Muslims.

text.p: Nike Inc. on Tuesday recalled more than 38,000 pairs of athletic shoes with a logo that outraged Moslems and apologised for what it called an unintentional offence.
The shoes sparked protests because the flame-shaped logo -- distinct from Nike's trademark "swoosh" logo -- looked like the Arabic word for "Allah," or God, company spokesman Roy Agostino said.
"There is in excess of 38,000 pairs in our distribution centres worldwide that we'll be recalling and we'll obliterate the logo before reintroducing it ... though our retail chain," Agostino said.
"Through a long process of discussions we have resolved our differences of opinion with the Moslem community," Nike said in a statement.

"While we never intended to offend -- we did. We have done everything possible to communicate our sincerest apologies and to address issues related to the distribution of any products offensive to the community," it said.
The recall affects a summer range of outdoor basketball products called Air Bakin, Air BBQ, Air Grill and Air Melt, which sell for $70 to $120 per pair.
Nike, based in Beaverton, Ore., has sold under a million pairs globally, it said.

Reacting to Nike's announcement, Malik Mujahid, a member of the Islamic Circle of North America, said, "We don't consider it a victory, more a realisation of a mistake. Nike and other organisations have not been very considerate in the past.

"We are happy that they (Nike managers) have finally decided that it was not something they wanted to promote in their products," he said in a telephone interview in Chicago. The Islamic Circle of North America provides locations for Friday prayers.
Agostino said the potential for trouble was suggested by one of the company's Moslem distributors in September.
"We immediately effected a design change to avoid confusion," he said.
However, Agostino said, in March the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CARE) alerted the company of concerns among members of the Islamic community.

Agostino said Nike tried to mitigate the impact on the Moslem community. "We diverted shipments away from Islamic states and completely discontinued the product range so no future product would be made as of March," he said.
Nike said it also made organisational changes in March to prevent a reccurence and to start testing Islamic sensibilites regarding its products.
"We wanted to bridge the gap and to take measures to allay concerns," he said, adding, "we were able to reach that understating with CARE on the measures.
He said Nike would not be taking any charge to earnings related to the recall.
Nike's class B stock rose $1.25 to $60 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
